title: The Skyline Problem
statement:
A city's skyline is the outer contour of the silhouette formed by all the buildings in that city when viewed from a distance.
Given the locations and heights of all the buildings, return the skyline formed by these buildings collectively.
The geometric information of each building is given in the array `buildings` where `buildings[i] = [lefti, righti, heighti]`.
The output must be a list of "key points" (sorted by x coordinate) in the format `[x, y]` that uniquely defines a skyline. A key point is the left endpoint of a horizontal line segment.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer N (number of buildings).
Next N lines: three space-separated integers left, right, height.
outputFormat: Print exactly one line per key point, space-separated x and y.

examples.explanation: Adjacent buildings with same height merge into one.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
buildings = [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
